featured_reviews.review_text:
My opinion is not very positive about this petrol pump and CNG station.
Everyone may have different opinions about the same place. So I would urge you to consider my experience as my personal feedback, and based on your sole experience, try to reach to a conclusion.
The major aspects, I considered are:
Location : 10/10
CNG Availability : 8/10
Service : 6/10
Genuineness : 6/10
Behavior : 3/10
Neatness : 3/10
Staff : 3/10
Queue : 4/10

This place is mostly crowded and always you may experience a long queue either for CNG or for Petrol and Diesel ⛽.

Now the next thing is staff behavior. Which is normally very rude with almost all the customers. You may often experience drunk staff at this station. And with drunken staff, it is difficult to expect genuine behavior.

Neatness is the third aspect which can be discussed separately. And at this level, this place deserves almost a negative review.
Try to use their washroom, you may experience vomiting 🤮🤢 . It is almost the same as any public toilet. The same situation is for a fuel refilling area. Considering its locality and crowd, it can be compared with a local garage.

Queues are another aspect which can be discussed separately. And in my opinion it is mostly because of mismanagement.

For petroleum and CNG, we all look for a local solution and this is the advantage for this place. It is open 24 x 7 for service.

But the management really needs to work seriously on above suggested points.

Thanks You.🙏

featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very bad experience at this petrol pump today. The staff here are extremely dishonest.

I clearly asked them to fill petrol worth ₹2000. The attendant deliberately asked me to park my car ahead of the machine where the meter was not clearly visible. Although I stepped out and checked that the meter was reset to zero before they started, something still felt off.
The moment I sat back in my car, the attendant immediately said the tank was filled. I found it suspicious because it normally takes time to fill petrol worth ₹2000. Instead of leaving, I reversed my car and checked the meter myself — it showed only ₹1602.
When I confronted him, he went completely silent and then filled the remaining ₹400.
This is a clear attempt to cheat customers. Please be very careful if you visit this petrol pump — always check the meter properly and do not trust blindly.
I will also be filing a complaint in the consumer court regarding this incident.

featured_reviews.review_text:
🚨Scammers 🚨

Please stay alert if you visit this petrol pump. Always check that the meter is at zero before fueling starts and keep an eye on the final amount and liters.

Today (24 May 2026) while returning from NESCO, we stopped here they asked us to move the car ahead and started fueling without properly showing the zero reading. Later, while one person distracted us by cleaning the windshield, another came with a payment machine showing ₹3500, even though the meter amount was ₹3062.

When we questioned him first he said fuel prices has been raised and this is the right amount but when we asked meter slip he suddenly said it was a mistake as he showed a diesel slip instead.

Please be very careful, avoid distractions, and always verify the meter and bill before paying.

featured_reviews.name: Dhriti Menon
featured_reviews.review_text: I had a very disappointing experience at the Hindustan Petroleum near aarey Colony. Yesterday, we paid ₹1000 for petrol, but only ₹700 worth was initially filled without informing us. When we questioned this and asked for the bill, the staff casually admitted that the remaining ₹300 hadn’t been filled yet. The person who originally took our money walked away without saying a word, which felt highly suspicious. Only after we called another staff member did he acknowledge the remaining amount and complete the filling. Even then, we were given two separate bills. This felt like a clear attempt to mislead or scam customers, and had we not been alert, we could have easily lost money. Please be very cautious while refueling here and always double-check the meter and bill before leaving.

featured_reviews.review_text:
### Mahanagar Gas CNG Station, Aarey Road, Goregaon East: A Detailed Review

The Mahanagar Gas CNG Station on Aarey Road, Goregaon East, is a well-equipped fuel station offering CNG, petrol, and diesel, along with additional services like a free air pump, a paid nitrogen pump, and lube oils. While the station itself is functional and provides all essential services, accessing it presents significant challenges that affect the overall convenience and safety.

### Accessibility Issues
Reaching the Mahanagar Gas CNG Station is notably difficult due to its location relative to the Western Express Highway (WEH). If you are approaching from the north side, there is no direct left turn into Aarey Road from the highway. Instead, drivers must continue past the Oberoi Mall flyover, take a service lane, and navigate back to reach the station. This detour can be time-consuming, often taking no less than 20 minutes due to traffic and multiple signals.

Similarly, for those coming from the south side, the journey is equally cumbersome. Drivers need to pass under the Oberoi Mall flyover and take a U-turn, adding to the travel time and causing delays. The combination of traffic signals and the busy nature of the area around the flyover exacerbates the problem, making what should be a quick stop a prolonged ordeal.

### Safety Concerns
The absence of a direct left cut from the northbound lane of WEH also raises serious safety concerns. Many drivers, in an attempt to save time, take dangerous shortcuts by crossing into the wrong lane after descending from the Oberoi Mall flyover to make an illegal U-turn. This risky maneuver poses a significant hazard, increasing the likelihood of accidents with vehicles traveling on the service lane from the north. The situation highlights a critical need for better traffic management and enforcement to prevent these unsafe practices.

### Fuel Station Services
Once you manage to reach the Mahanagar Gas CNG Station, the service is generally satisfactory. The station offers a full range of fuels—CNG, petrol, and diesel—catering to a variety of vehicles. Additionally, there is a free air pump available for tire inflation, along with a paid nitrogen pump for those who prefer it. Lube oils are also available, making it a convenient one-stop shop for various automotive needs.

### Conclusion
The Mahanagar Gas CNG Station on Aarey Road is a well-equipped fuel stop with all the essential services you would expect, including CNG, petrol, diesel, air, nitrogen, and lube oils. However, the major drawback is the challenging and time-consuming access route, whether you are approaching from the north or south on WEH. The safety risks posed by drivers taking illegal shortcuts to reach the station further complicate the situation. While the station itself is adequate, the accessibility and safety issues significantly impact the overall convenience and could benefit from better traffic management solutions.

🚨 Beware of the Air Pump Scam! 🚨
Next time you stop to fill air in your tyres, stay alert. A common trick is happening at some air pumps:

🔧 The man filling air will secretly loosen the tyre valve.
💨 Air slowly leaks out…
⚠️ Then he tells you, “tyre is punctured.”

Right beside the pump, another person (part of the same scam) will quickly offer to “fix” it and charge ₹200–₹300 to replace the valve — even though nothing was actually wrong.

🛑 How to protect yourself:
• Watch closely while air is being filled
• Check the valve yourself before agreeing to any repair
• Don’t rush into paying for “quick fixes”
• If possible, fill air yourself

👉 Stay alert. Share this post to help others avoid getting scammed!

On 15 June 2026, I filled petrol and the staff initially told me the bill amount was around ₹3,491. I was surprised because I had observed the meter and expected the amount to be around ₹2,700. After questioning them, they produced a bill showing ₹3,391, and I ended up paying the amount through UPI.

Later, when I reached home and checked the receipt carefully, I noticed that the receipt time was 20:41, whereas my UPI payment was made at 21:13. This clearly indicated that the receipt did not belong to my transaction. I immediately returned to the petrol pump, and after discussion, the staff admitted it was a "mistake" and refunded the excess amount.

What makes this even more suspicious is that during a previous visit, I witnessed another customer arguing that petrol had not been filled into his vehicle despite being charged.

Such incidents raise serious concerns about transparency and customer trust. Customers should carefully verify the meter reading, receipt details, and transaction amount before making payment. The management and authorities should investigate these repeated complaints and take strict action if any fraudulent practices are found.

I have preserved the receipt and payment proof and will continue to raise this issue with the appropriate authorities if necessary.

Date of Incident: 15 June 2026
Location: Anuradha Gas Station, JVLR, Andheri East, Mumbai

featured_reviews.review_text:
I usually prefer filling petrol at Indian Oil petrol pumps, but yesterday I had a rather disappointing experience. While returning home, I stopped at this petrol station to fill fuel in my car.

The man filling the petrol suddenly started asking, “Where in UP are you from?” At first, we thought he was speaking to someone else, but when he repeated the question, Arvind — my brother’s friend who was driving — replied, “Varanasi.” After that, he continued asking more personal questions, and in the middle of the conversation, he suddenly said, “Auto cut ho gaya hai.”

We had asked for petrol worth ₹1005, but when I looked carefully, the meter had already shown two lines before the filling even started. He then claimed the machine had auto-cut at ₹840 and returned the remaining amount because I had already paid ₹1005 in advance. Even while returning the balance, the amount was ₹5 short.

What felt even stranger was that once we started driving, the fuel indicator in the car barely moved up. Only God knows what actually happened.

Overall, the entire experience left me feeling cheated and deeply disappointed. It is sad how, at times, people compromise their honesty and integrity for such small gains. Trust is something customers carry with them when they stop at a fuel station, and once broken, it leaves a very unpleasant feeling behind.

Ironically, my name is also Anuradha, and coincidentally, the gas station was called “Anuradha Gas Station.”
